Full inference-pipeline executable: load the locally-shipped causal LM + BPE tokenizer (local_files_only=True) and run a forward cross-entropy (CE) loss reading the LM's vocab size; build HearthNet from a fixed checkpoint whose tensors are exactly (10,784) and (10,10) with matching biases; implement a bag-MIL forward (encoder + attention gate + MLP returning logits and attention) and a policy/WDL head emitting legal-move logits plus a post-softmax outcome vector; pack the request stream into aligned microbatches under per-micro batch token-window and batch-count budgets; run the microbatch compute in all-forward-all-backward (AFAB) order with no forward after any backward; rescale each microbatch pooled loss by its microbatch-count share and accumulate gradients so the total grad equals the reference that averages over microbatches; ship every weight byte-for-byte unchanged with fixed shapes. dependent_stages=3: load -> tokenize -> MIL/policy forward -> microbatch packing -> AFDB backward -> loss/grad emission fail together. quantitative_correctness=3: the emitted loss and accumulated gradient norms must match (within float tolerance) the golden values computed from the frozen checkpoint for each scenario. adversarial_inputs=3 and hidden_case_generalization=3: the four hidden scenarios exercise an oversized variant forced into its own microbatch, every-microbatched-singleton, singleton (1-instance) and zero-span bags, and large bursts, so the same infer.py must generalise. The three hard-floor competencies (C-a633e294 loss scaling + gradient accumulation, C-a781c612 AFAB scheduling, C-dc8c9187 policy/WDL head) keep the task at hard regardless of the medium/easy medium other floors.
